The error lies in the subsequent steps or the search result interpretation (likely mixing up the subject with his father, Napoléon Alexandre Berthier, who was actually the one famously associated with the title Prince of Wagram, while the 3rd Prince was his son, though the specific dates in Turn 3 suggest a search error rather than a planning error). Therefore, the planning step itself was not flawed; the flaw was in the information retrieval or synthesis phase. The analysis incorrectly blames the planning logic.
